I have farmed these 8.5 mu for 30 years. I know every corner of my land. I am 50 now, and my bones tell me when the weather is turning. My household has seven people. My sons work off-farm in the city and send money home, so I can afford good seed and fertilizer, but we are short on hands during busy times. That is why I rely on my well and my experience—I cannot wait for rain or for others to tell me what to do.

My plan is the same one that has fed my family for decades, with small adjustments based on what I saw last year. I keep 6 mu for my wheat-maize rotation. Wheat is already in the ground from last October. I will topdress urea at green-up and again at jointing, irrigate three times from my well, and watch for rust and aphids. After harvest in early June, there is no time to waste. I will rotary till that same day and put in hybrid maize seed. Maize needs heat and water at the right moments, so I will irrigate twice and side-dress fertilizer at the big trumpet stage.

On 2 mu I grow cotton. It is our old crop here in Quzhou. I plant improved Bt cotton in late April. Cotton brings steady money, but it is greedy for labor and water. I will give it four irrigations and spray three times for aphids and spider mites. The remaining 0.5 mu I plant mungbean with a traditional local variety. It is for home consumption and a little cash at market. It does not need much—some phosphorus and potash, one irrigation if the summer turns dry, and one spray.

I use rotary tillage for the summer crops because it is fast. With my family working away, I cannot spend days ploughing with animals or walking tractors. My well is my advantage. I do not fear dry spells like some of my neighbors do.
